items.title: Two siblings’ bodies recovered in Mirpur canal, search for third child called off
items.description: JHELUM: The bodies of two siblings, who were allegedly thrown into a canal by their father in Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, were recovered on Thursday, while the rescue operation for the third child was abandoned without recovering his body, a rescue official said. Mirpur District Emergency Officer (DEO) Sardar Najam Sadozai said that Rescue-1122 divers were conducting an operation to recover the third child’s body from the Khari Sharif canal in Mirpur. However, in a later update, he confirmed that rescue officials had stopped the operation without recovering the third child’s body. The Khari Sharif canal originates from the Jhelum River and is located in the border area between AJK’s Mirpur and the Mangla Dam canal in Punjab’s Jhelum district. Jhelum District Police Officer (DPO) Shafiq Chaudhry confirmed that police had arrested a man, for allegedly throwing his three children — two daughters and a son — into a canal in Mirpur. According to preliminary investigations, the suspect was allegedly an addict and had an estranged relationship with his wife, who had been living at her paternal home. Further investigation was underway, DPO Chaudhry said. “Police in Jhelum are investigating the suspect from all possible angles to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of the children,” he added. The suspect confessed to the crime after his wife raised an alarm over the disappearance of their three children, the senior police official added. According to DPO Chaudhry, the suspect had taken his three children with him “for an outing” but did not return. “As the suspect is also an addict, his wife became alarmed when the children did not return and informed the police,” he said. “The Mangla police station in Jhelum district, taking notice of the complaint, took the man into custody, where he told police that he had thrown his three children into a canal of the Jhelum River,” the senior official said. The police registered a first information report (FIR) on the complaint of the children’s mother under Section 363 of the Pakistan Penal Code. “On September 15, 2026, at around 6pm, I, along with my brother, took the children to Pir Bhechan Darbar for a visit. On our return, my brother stopped the vehicle in front of a bakery on Mangla Road in Dina, and I went to buy some items for the children. “While I was inside the bakery, my husband, Zeeshan, accompanied by two unidentified individuals, approached my brother’s vehicle in my absence and told him: ‘I am going to the City Housing Society; I will take the children with me to the park and return them to you afterwards.’ “Persuaded by his words, my brother handed all three children over to Zeeshan. Shortly afterwards, both my brother and I became deeply concerned.” The complainant added that when she tried to contact the suspect on his mobile phone, it was switched off. She further said that she and her brother then searched for the children to the best of their ability but were unable to find them.

items.title: 2027: Why Tinubu should be given second term — Lalong, First Lady
items.description: —Gains from reforms must be secured for future generations — First Lady –As ex-Plateau governor says subsidy removal painful but necessary By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA —FORMER Plateau State Governor, Senator Simon Lalong and First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu on Thursday urged Nigerians to sustain President Bola Tinubu’s reform agenda beyond 2027, saying the tough measures already rolled out need more time to yield their full benefits. As Lalong asked Nigerians to re-elect the president in 2027 to allow him finish his reforms, the First Lady emphasized the need to consolidate the administration’s achievements for the benefit of today’s and tomorrow’s citizens. They spoke at the National Summit of the Forum of All Progressives Congress Former Presiding Officers of State Houses of Assembly of Nigeria (APC-FOPSHAN), held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. The forum, attended by former and serving presiding officers of state legislatures and other political stakeholders, was held under the theme, “Bold Leadership, Bold Reforms: From Subsidy to Renewed Hope.” Senator Lalong, who was a former Speaker of the Plateau State House of Assembly, argued that President Tinubu had demonstrated the courage to confront structural economic problems previous administrations had struggled to resolve, particularly the petrol subsidy regime. According to him: “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has exemplified those bold steps and come 2027, Nigerians will reward him to complete the great work.” Senator Lalong, who was a special guests of honour at the event stated that the President chose economic reform over political convenience by announcing the removal of petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, despite the immediate consequences for households and businesses. “For decades, Nigeria consumed what we did not produce. We succeeded in making our future children pay for cheap petrol,” he said. “Everyone knew the truth but no leader had the courage to confront it.” He said subsidy removal represented one of the most difficult economic decisions taken in recent years, but its significance went beyond ending government expenditure on subsidised petrol. “It was not an easy decision. It was not a political convenient decision. But sometimes, leadership is tested not by the decisions that are easy to make, but by the courage to make decisions that the moment demands,” he said. He said the fundamental question confronting the country was how to redirect public resources from consumption towards investments capable of expanding productive capacity. “The real significance of subsidy removal therefore is not simply that one subsidy disappeared. It is that Nigeria has been compelled to confront a fundamental question: how do we move from consuming public resources to investing these resources in productive capacity for our nation?” Lalong said. The former governor said political leaders must also accept responsibility for explaining the rationale behind the reforms to Nigerians rather than leaving the government alone to defend difficult policy choices. “Our duty today goes beyond assessment. Our duty is to be ambassadors of this difficult but necessary reform,” he said. “President Tinubu has done his part by taking the bold decision. Our part is to help our people understand that the pains of today are the gains of tomorrow. “We must tell Nigerians that bold leadership is not about being popular today, it is about being right for society.” Lalong said the next challenge was ensuring that resources made available through the reforms were invested in sectors capable of expanding production, creating jobs and improving living standards. “We must invest in agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure, education, energy, and technology,” he said. According to him, Nigeria must create an environment in which citizens can produce more, businesses can expand and young people can access meaningful economic opportunities. He also placed responsibility on the legislature, saying lawmakers must scrutinise government expenditure, strengthen oversight and ensure that citizens’ concerns remain central to the implementation of the reforms. Lalong called for greater fiscal responsibility, stronger democratic institutions and sustained efforts to strengthen the autonomy and capacity of national institutions. He said history would judge the current period by how political leaders responded to Nigeria’s longstanding structural challenges. “This is one of those periods President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has chosen the path of reform. The road has required difficult decisions, but the responsibility of leadership is not to avoid every difficulty. It is to confront the structural challenges that have held the country back and begin the work of building something more sustainable,” he said. Lalong described the administration’s reform journey as an attempt to move Nigeria away from dependency, consumption and short-term interventions towards productivity, investment and long-term economic transformation. “The journey from subsidy to Renewed Hope is a journey from dependency to productivity, from consumption to investment, and from short-term fix to long-term economic transformation,” he said. “It is a journey that requires courage from the executive, responsibility from the legislatures, discipline across government and patience from the people.” He added: “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated the courage to begin this difficult journey. Our responsibility is to ensure that reforms succeed, that their gains are consolidated, and that Nigerians emerge stronger, more productive, more prosperous.” The First Lady, who was Special Guest of Honour, similarly said the administration had been working to reposition the economy and establish foundations for sustainable national development. “Since the inception of this administration, Mr. President has worked tirelessly to reposition our economy and lay a solid foundation for sustainable national development,” Mrs Tinubu said. “Nation-building is a continuous process, and the gains already recorded must be consolidated for the benefit of present and future generations.” She also welcomed the forum’s endorsement of President Tinubu for a second term, saying the support carried particular significance because it came from former legislative leaders familiar with the demands of governance and the difficulties associated with major policy decisions. “I especially acknowledge and appreciate your endorsement of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for a second term in office. Coming from men and women who have themselves presided over legislative institutions, your endorsement carries special significance,” she said. “You understand the demands of governance, the difficulty of making critical decisions, and the courage required to pursue reforms in the national interest.” The First Lady added: “On behalf of Mr. President, I thank you for this expression of confidence, support and goodwill.” Mrs Tinubu also challenged former Speakers and Deputy Speakers not to withdraw from public service simply because they had left elective office, saying the country still required their institutional experience and networks. “Leaving political office should never mean leaving public service. Nigeria still needs your wisdom, experience, and networks,” she said. She urged them to use the forum to preserve institutional memory, mentor younger legislators, promote democratic stability and continue contributing to development in communities where they had served. The First Lady, who accepted her designation as Grand Patron of the forum, commended its National Chairman, Senator Wasiu Sanni-Eshilokun, Board of Trustees and leadership for bringing former legislative leaders together. She expressed hope that the summit would strengthen cooperation among members and create a platform for continued contributions to national unity and democratic development. “May this Summit strengthen the bonds among you and open a new chapter of meaningful contribution to our nation, promote national unity and strengthen our democracy,” she said. Lalong, said sustaining the reforms required commitment across government and patience from citizens. “The time for bold leadership is now. The time for bold reform is now. And the time to build a stronger, more productive and more prosperous Nigeria is now,” he said. The post 2027: Why Tinubu should be given second term — Lalong, First Lady appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Twenty-Five Political Prisoners Released, Deported from Belarus
items.description: Click to expand Image TOR BAND musicians, former political prisoners, embrace their loved ones after arriving in Vilnius on September 16, 2026. © 2026 Human Rights Watch This week 25 former political prisoners arrived in Vilnius, Lithuania having been released from detention in Belarus. Their release was negotiated by the United States special envoy to Belarus John Coale with president Aliaksander Lukashenka. In exchange, the US lifted sanctions on two Belarusian companies. Among those released are journalist Andrei Aleksandrau and activist Iryna Zlobina, who married while in detention; lawyer Anastasiya Lazarenka, prosecuted for organizing legal consultations, among other charges; activist Alena Lazarchyk, a single parent whose communication with her child was limited by the prison management; and Sviatlana Yakubovich, a volunteer at Viasna, one of the leading human rights groups in Belarus. Most of them had been sentenced to harsh sentences of up to 14 years. Click to expand Image Former political prisoner Alena Lazarchyk after being brought to Vilnius from Belarus, September 16, 2026. © 2026 Human Rights Watch After her arrival in Vilnius, Lazarchyk told those gathered that she had not believed she would be freed until the very last moment. “One day, they say, ‘get your things.’ I was sure they were just transferring me somewhere, but they said I was being deported.” Belarusian authorities regularly impose forced expulsion as a mandatory condition for some political prisoners’ release, a practice which violates international human rights law, as United Nations experts have underscored. Since summer 2025, hundreds of political prisoners have been taken outside Belarus following their release from detention. Some have been deported without passports while others have reported that their passports were canceled following their expulsion from Belarus. While the release of these 25 prisoners is something to celebrate, at least 886 prisoners remain in jail in Belarus on politically motivated grounds. Every month, dozens more are detained and handed heavy prison sentences. According to Coale, the negotiations will continue and more political prisoners will be released soon. However Belarus' president persists with the false narrative that there are no political prisoners in Belarus. These prisoners aren’t gaming pieces to be exchanged for political favors. Governments need to increase the pressure on Belarusian authorities to end its ruthless, politically motivated crackdowns and to secure the freedom of the hundreds of political prisoners who continue to languish in jail, without exile from their home being the price they must pay.

items.title: Au Mali, les écoles se préparent à la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027
items.description: a deux semaines de la rentree scolaire 2026-2027, prevue le jeudi 1er octobre 2026 sur l'ensemble du territoire national, les preparatifs s'intensifient dans plusieurs etablissements scolaires au Mali. Nettoyage des salles, desherbage et reparation des tables bancs sont notamment au programme. Mais dans certaines ecoles occupees par des personnes deplacees, les preparatifs restent difficiles, voire impossibles. Dans le nord du Mali, certaines ecoles servent encore de lieux d'accueil aux populations deplacees par l'insecurite. a Tombouctou, le second cycle « La Paix » est toujours occupe par des familles deplacees venues de Zouera. Selon le directeur de l'etablissement, Alhousseini Harber Souleymane, les autorites travaillent a leur relogement sur un nouveau site. Un emplacement situe derriere l'abattoir aurait ete identifie et serait actuellement en cours d'amenagement. « Si la situation ne change pas, je pense qu'il n'y aura meme pas d'ecole. Parce que toutes les classes sont occupees. Donc, il faut forcement la liberation des classes pour que nous puissions faire quoi que ce soit. » Alhousseini Harber Souleymane precise par ailleurs que les salles de classe et le mobilier devront etre remis en etat apres le depart des deplaces, avant la reprise des cours. Au centre du pays, les preparatifs avancent a Bandiagara, la situation est differente. Les preparatifs de la rentree scolaire ont deja commence dans plusieurs etablissements. Au programme, nettoyage des salles de classe, desherbage et reparation des tables-bancs. a l'ecole Mamadou Tolo premier cycle B, les travaux sont meme presque termines, selon son directeur, Gouro Traore. « Nous avons commence le desherbage depuis une semaine. Souvent, il y a la crise des carburants, mais j'ai paye l'essence pour noircir les tableaux aussi. Et bientot, il y aura un menuisier qui va venir reparer les tables-bancs », precise monsieur Traore. Malgre les difficultes liees notamment a l'approvisionnement en carburant, l'etablissement poursuit donc ses preparatifs afin d'etre pret pour la reprise des cours. Une annee scolaire en trois trimestres Au Mali, l'annee scolaire 2026-2027 sera organisee en trois trimestres. Le premier trimestre s'etendra du 1er octobre au 23 decembre 2026, le deuxieme du 4 janvier au 24 mars 2027 et le troisieme du 5 avril au 30 juin 2027. a l'approche de la rentree, la situation des ecoles occupees par les personnes deplacees reste ainsi un enjeu important, notamment dans les zones affectees par l'insecurite. Lire aussi : Kayes : les ecoles se preparent pour la rentree scolaire L’article Au Mali, les écoles se préparent à la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Africa CDC warns Ebola outbreak not ‘under control’
items.description: An Ebola outbreak in DR Congo was far from being “under control”, Africa’s top health body said Thursday, a day after the WHO said it was gaining ground against the virus. The outbreak, which began in the conflict-scarred northeastern province of Ituri, has seen more than 3,500 deaths from over 7,200 cases to date across seven northern and eastern provinces. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) director general Jean Kaseya acknowledged there had been a “plateau” in cases, adding they were seeing “a slight decrease”. “And no one can come and say the outbreak is under control. No one,” he said. Kaseya’s remarks follow the head of the World Health Organization, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who on Wednesday said: “We are starting to see encouraging signs that we’re gaining ground.” On Saturday, the Democratic Republic of Congo government spokesman Patrick Muyaya said on X that “the peak was reached” in the third week of August. Kaseya said “some of the comments that were made were based on incomplete data”. The African Union places the current figures at 7,404 cases, with 3,577 cumulative deaths. Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and can cause severe internal and external bleeding and organ failure, has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years. There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment against the Bundibugyo strain responsible for the current outbreak. The post Africa CDC warns Ebola outbreak not ‘under control’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SSNIT urges pensioners to use digital channels to access services
items.description: The Deputy Director-General in charge of Operations and Benefits at the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), Adam Sulley, has urged pensioners to use the Trust’s digital channels and co-location branches to access services more conveniently. He said the introduction of these digital channels was part of broader reforms to modernise the Trust’s operations and offer innovative services to pensioners to help strengthen the sustainability of the scheme. He said this when the SSNIT engaged pensioners in the Western Region to educate them on some of the new reforms and policies introduced by the Trust as part of deepening pension literacy among retirees. The engagement, held in Takoradi, was on the theme: “ 60 years strong: Enhancing pensioners’ experience through improved service delivery .” Mr Sulley stated that the pensioners were their most valuable stakeholders, so it was crucial for SSNIT to connect with them as often as possible to ensure they stayed informed about the new developments happening in the Trust, especially with technology. “You would agree with me that pensioners and technology are not the best of friends, so there is no way we can leverage our technology if we do not engage them for them to know what is available to access our services conveniently for them,” he said. Touching on the co-location policy, he noted that SSNIT had partnered with Ecobank, GCB Bank, and Fidelity Bank to establish service points to bring pension services closer to the doorsteps of pensioners, contributors, and members. “If a pensioner wants to go to an SSNIT branch, they do not have to travel long distances. They can enter Ecobank, GCB Bank, and Fidelity Bank branches near them and they will access the same services there with ease,” Mr Sulley added. He, therefore, asked the pensioners to make use of the Trust’s digital services and co-location service points nationwide to renew their pensioner certificates, and access all other services at the comfort of their homes without stress. He also said that, as part of new pension packages, the SSNIT, in collaboration with the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) and The Trust Hospital, had developed Telehealth Services to provide healthcare services for pensioners through digital platforms. “We need to let them know that we have introduced Telehealth where they can access a medical facility in the comfort of their locations, and all they need to do is dial a dedicated toll-free number and a doctor will be available to take them through consultations and give them prescriptions,” Mr Sulley said. The Western Regional Chairman of the National Pensioners Association, Anthony Essien, expressed gratitude to the SSNIT for engaging them on matters of importance to their welfare. “We have learnt a lot, and what we are being told here gives us a new dimension into the operations of SSNIT, and I believe that we will adjust to the new things we have heard so that we can help SSNIT to better take care of our welfare as pensioners,” he said.

items.title: Pakistan ranked among bottom three in WEF's Global Gender Gap Report 2026
items.description: Pakistan ranked third-to-last in the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Global Gender Gap Report 2026, with 59.5 per cent gender parity, up almost 3pc from last year . The annual report benchmarked the current state and evolution of gender parity across four key dimensions: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. Pakistan scored the lowest out of the 38 lower-middle-income economies, as well as the seven South Asian countries, included in the report. “While Pakistan remains among the lowest-ranked economies in the index, it has nonetheless narrowed its gender gap over time by 5.2 percentage points, up from 54.3pc in 2006,” the report said. “Furthermore, the 2026 edition marks its strongest year-on-year improvement in a decade, driven primarily by substantial gains in educational attainment.” Economic participation and opportunity Pakistan ranked 144th in economic participation and opportunity in 2026, moving up three places from its 147th rank in the same index in 2025. The report revealed that 81.46pc of men participated in the labour force, compared to only 28.21pc of women. According to the report, an overwhelming 93.87pc of legislators, senior officials and managers in Pakistan’s workforce were men, compared to women making up 6.13pc. For the professional and technical workers category, the gap was lower with 30.96pc of the positions being occupied by women. The country ranked 115th in wage equality for similar work and 140th in estimated earned income. The report also revealed that 4.9pc of firms in Pakistan had a female majority ownership, while only 3.4pc firms had female top managers. Educational attainment Pakistan ranked 130th in educational attainment, marking a substantial gain in the category. Male literacy rate in the country was reported to be at 69.14pc, while female literacy rate stood at 48.52pc. Boys’ enrolment in primary education was at 83.01pc compared to 81.08pc among girls. In secondary education, male enrolment stood at 49.99pc, compared to 46.48pc in female enrolment. Pakistan ranked first in the world for enrolment in tertiary education, marking high parity, as 10.71pc of women and 11.01pc of men were enrolled. Health and survival The country ranked 127th in the health and survival category. Within the category, Pakistan ranked first in sex ratio at birth, showing high parity between male and female births. Male healthy life expectancy stood at 57.1pc, compared to 56.69pc for women. Political empowerment Pakistan ranked 107th globally in the political empowerment index. According to the report, 78.31pc of parliamentarians were men, compared to 21.69pc being women. Further, an overwhelming 96.55pc of individuals in ministerial positions were men, compared to only 3.45pc of positions being occupied by women. With a female head of state having ruled the country for 4.73 of the last 50 years, Pakistan ranked 39th in this subindex. Access to finance, justice The report also revealed that women in Pakistan didn’t enjoy equal rights regarding inheritance for widows and daughters. It added that women had “near-equal rights” when it came to access to financial services, land assets and non-land assets. According to the report, women had “restricted rights” when it came to access to justice, while they had “equal rights” for freedom of movement. The report also said that women in Pakistan had “unequal rights” for right to divorce. It added that 24.9pc of women had experienced gendered violence in their lives, and that women in Pakistan had “restricted rights” regarding their reproductive autonomy.

items.title: Burkina : Africa Mousso célèbre dix ans d’engagement en faveur des femmes dès le 20 octobre
items.description: BURKINA-FEMMES-AFRICA-MOUSSO-ANNIVERSAIRE Burkina : Africa Mousso célèbre dix ans d’engagement en faveur des femmes dès le 20 octobre Ouagadougou, 17 sept. 2026 (AIB) – L’initiative panafricaine Africa Mousso célébrera, du 20 au 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, ses dix ans d’engagement en faveur des femmes battantes, autour des enjeux liés à la paix, à la cohésion sociale et au développement de la femme, a annoncé jeudi sa présidente fondatrice, Sandrine Folané/Ouédraogo. La célébration sera marquée par plusieurs activités, notamment une cérémonie de lancement officiel, un forum au Ciné Burkina, une exposition du 20 au 22 octobre et une soirée de distinctions et de gala, le 23 octobre à la salle des Banquets de Ouaga 2000. Selon la promotrice, Sandrine Folané/Ouédraogo le forum réunira des femmes et des hommes autour de plusieurs thématiques liées notamment à la paix, à la cohésion sociale et au développement de la femme. Des formations seront également organisées au profit d’au moins une centaine de jeunes filles dans différents domaines, notamment la teinture, la décoration et le tissage de paille. « Africa Mousso est dédié aux femmes du secteur informel », a déclaré Sandrine Folané/Ouédraogo, citant notamment les coiffeuses, les transformatrices de légumes et de jus, les commerçantes et les autres femmes qui se lèvent tôt pour travailler. L’initiative, lancée en 2016, vise à mettre en lumière des femmes qui, selon la promotrice, restent souvent dans l’ombre alors qu’elles contribuent au fonctionnement de la société et à l’économie nationale. « À l’époque, les distinctions étaient davantage attribuées aux autorités et aux femmes ministres. Je me suis demandé pourquoi ne pas honorer également les femmes de l’autre facette, celles du secteur informel », a-t-elle expliqué. Pour cette dixième édition, le Mali, le Niger et la Guinée sont annoncés comme pays invités d’honneur. Des femmes battantes venues de ces pays participeront notamment au forum et à la soirée gala. Un don sera également effectué, à l’issue de la manifestation, au profit des veuves des Forces de défense et de sécurité tombées. La soirée du 23 octobre sera consacrée à la distinction de plusieurs femmes dans différentes catégories, notamment à travers le prix de la Femme impact, le prix de l’Intégration africaine et de la résilience féminine, le prix Femme AES, le prix Maman Africa courage et le prix Femme réfugiée inspirante. Des prix seront également décernés dans les domaines de la santé, de l’éducation et du monde rural. Le grand prix, dénommé « prix Sanem paaga », sera doté de 1,5 million de FCFA, tandis qu’un deuxième prix de 500 000 FCFA sera attribué selon le vote du public et la visibilité des candidates sur les réseaux sociaux. Depuis 2016, Africa Mousso affirme avoir honoré plus de 300 femmes dans plusieurs catégories et dans différentes localités, notamment Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso et Koudougou. Grâce à l’accompagnement de ses partenaires, l’initiative dit avoir mobilisé plus de 17 millions de FCFA au profit des femmes et formé plus de 1 000 bénéficiaires depuis sa création. Elle revendique également un impact de plus de deux millions de femmes à travers ses réseaux. « Dix ans, ce n’est pas dix jours. Pour moi, dix ans, c’est une grâce », a déclaré la promotrice, rappelant les difficultés rencontrées au cours du parcours. « À la troisième édition, j’ai failli abandonner, mais l’amour pour cette cause m’a poussée à continuer », a-t-elle confié. La promotrice a, par ailleurs, appelé les partenaires à accompagner davantage les initiatives destinées aux femmes du secteur informel, promettant que des témoignages vidéo de femmes ayant bénéficié de dons et d’appuis seront diffusés au cours de la célébration des dix ans d’Africa Mousso. items.title: Photos: Ghana hosts Japanese astronaut for talks on space science and technology
items.description: Ghana has hosted Japanese astronaut and Axiom Space Chief Technology Officer for Asia Pacific, Dr Koichi Wakata, for discussions on strengthening cooperation in space science, technology and innovation. Dr Wakata’s engagement with Ghanaian officials and institutions forms part of his visit to the country from September 15 to 19, 2026, aimed at promoting knowledge exchange and exploring opportunities for collaboration in space-related fields. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa hosted Dr Wakata at a dinner at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Tuesday, September 15, following a courtesy call on the Minister. Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry was ready to support international partnerships that advance Ghana’s national and strategic objectives. He stressed the importance of international cooperation in space exploration, noting that countries, scientists, engineers and institutions needed to work together to advance the sector. The Minister also highlighted Ghana’s longstanding relations with Japan, noting that 2027 will mark 70 years of formal diplomatic relations between the two countries. Chief Director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Khadija Iddrisu, said space technologies and satellite data were already supporting areas including communications, agriculture, environmental monitoring, disaster management and national security. She said Ghana needed to strengthen its capacity to make effective use of these technologies and described Dr Wakata’s visit as an opportunity for knowledge exchange and greater interest in space science and technology. Japanese Ambassador to Ghana, Hiroshi Yoshimoto, recalled Japan’s support for Ghana’s space programme, particularly the launch of Ghana’s first satellite. He said Dr Wakata’s visit provided an opportunity for Ghana and Japan to build on that experience and explore further cooperation in science, technology and space-related areas. University of Ghana Vice-Chancellor, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, also highlighted the university’s longstanding collaboration with Japan in research, science and capacity development. She said the university was ready to expand partnerships in science, technology and innovation, while welcoming Dr Wakata’s planned interaction with students and researchers. Dr Wakata shared his journey into space, saying his interest began at the age of five after watching the Apollo 11 Moon landing. He has completed five space flights and spent a cumulative 504 days in space, flying aboard the Space Shuttle, the Russian Soyuz spacecraft and SpaceX’s Crew Dragon. He encouraged young people to pursue careers in science, technology and engineering and highlighted the role of international collaboration in advancing space research. Dr Wakata also spoke about sustainability in space, including the recycling of resources aboard the International Space Station and the need to address the growing problem of space debris. Students of Presbyterian Boys’ Secondary School (PRESEC), Legon, winners of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz, also attended the dinner and interacted with Dr Wakata. His visit continues until September 19, with further engagements expected to focus on knowledge exchange and opportunities for Ghana-Japan cooperation in space science, technology and innovation. items.title: Customs intercepts police uniforms, pistol, explosives in Oyo
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo/Osun Area Command of the Nigeria Customs Service, NCS, has intercepted 573 Nigeria Police Force crests, 92 yards of police camouflage uniform fabric, a pistol, six pistol magazines, a pump-action magazine and 60 detonating cords during its anti-smuggling operations in August 2026. The Acting Customs Area Controller of the command, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Wale Moses Adewole, disclosed this on Thursday in Ibadan while briefing journalists on the command’s revenue performance and anti-smuggling activities. Adewole said the interception of the police-related materials raised security concerns because of the unauthorised possession and movement of security agency uniforms and insignia. He said the materials could potentially be misused for impersonation or unauthorised access to restricted areas. “Of particular concern was the interception of police crest and camouflage uniforms. The unauthorised possession and movement of security agency uniforms can create serious security concerns, particularly in view of the prevailing security challenges in the country,” Adewole said. He said the command would continue to pay attention to items with potential implications for national security and public safety. According to him, the command also intercepted a pistol, six pistol magazines, a pump-action magazine and 60 detonating cords during the period under review. Other items seized included 2,012 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, 550 bags of 25kg foreign parboiled rice, 2,440 wraps of cannabis sativa, 1,150 used tyres, 101 used compressors and 48 packs of 225mg tramadol. The list of intercepted goods also included 105 bales and 28 sacks of used clothing, 18 sacks of used shoes, 450 25-litre kegs of Premium Motor Spirit, equivalent to 5,000 litres, 33 three-litre bottles of foreign vegetable oil and 30 bags of foreign sugar weighing 60kg each. The command further seized 17 used vehicles, commonly referred to as tokunbo vehicles, 10 means of conveyance and 10 containers of corrosive mercury. Adewole said the seizures had a cumulative Duty Paid Value of N4,106,951,689. He explained that the interceptions were part of the command’s statutory responsibility to prevent the smuggling of prohibited and restricted goods. “In line with our statutory responsibility to protect the nation’s economy and prevent the smuggling of prohibited and restricted goods, the Command has continued to intensify its anti-smuggling operations across its areas of jurisdiction,” he said. The acting controller said the interception of mercury was also significant because of the potential risks associated with improper handling, storage or transportation of the substance. He said uncontrolled movement of such materials could pose risks including fire, explosion, injury and property damage. “The uncontrolled movement of such materials can expose members of the public to risks of fire, explosion, injury, property damage, and, in extreme circumstances, loss of lives,” Adewole said. Adewole attributed the seizures to the vigilance of officers and men of the command, intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with sister security agencies and other relevant stakeholders. He said the command would sustain its anti-smuggling operations while ensuring that legitimate businesses and law-abiding members of the public were not subjected to unnecessary impediments. Revenue performance On revenue generation, Adewole disclosed that the Oyo/Osun Area Command generated N65,661,343,026.94 between January and August 2026. He said the figure represented a 13.88 per cent increase over the N57,656,161,990.24 collected during the corresponding period in 2025. The acting controller attributed the improved revenue performance to the command’s efforts in revenue collection, trade facilitation, stakeholder engagement and strategies aimed at improving compliance. “I am pleased to inform you that between January and August 2026, the Command generated a total revenue of Sixty Five Billion, Six Hundred and Sixty-One Million, Three Hundred and Forty-Three Thousand, Twenty-Six Naira, Ninety-Four Kobo,” he said. Adewole said the command remained committed to improving revenue generation, facilitating legitimate trade and sustaining its anti-smuggling operations. He assured residents and legitimate businesses within the command’s jurisdiction that the Customs Service would continue to balance enforcement with trade facilitation. “We will continue to pay particular attention to items that have implications for national security and public safety, while ensuring that legitimate businesses and law-abiding members of the public are not unduly impeded,” he said. Adewole also pledged that the command would continue to discharge its responsibilities professionally and in accordance with the provisions of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023. He commended journalists for their continued partnership with the Nigeria Customs Service and urged the media to sustain responsible reportage of the activities of the service. items.title: Death toll tops 80 in West Kordofan mine disaster as rescue effort falters
items.description: At least 80 people have died after a gold mine collapsed near El Nahud in West Kordofan, according to a local administration official. A further 50 people are injured, while the number still trapped underground remains unknown. The collapse at El Zara mine, in the Foga administrative unit west of El Nahud, occurred on Sunday evening. Rescue efforts are being carried out with rudimentary equipment, the official says, while the mine’s sandy terrain has triggered further collapses. Surviving miners say they do not know how many people remain trapped in the mine’s shafts. Earlier reports put the combined number of dead and missing at more than 70, while the Sudan Doctors Network reported at least 67 deaths as rescue operations continued. The latest figure of 82 deaths was given by a West Kordofan local administration official, who also confirmed 50 injuries. Civilian resue efforts after the collapse of El Zara mine near En Nuhud (Photo: Supplied) Slow rescue effort, no official response Murtada Ahmed, spokesman for the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory, tells Radio Dabanga that search and rescue operations are proceeding extremely slowly, with almost no specialised equipment available for such an accident. Local residents and miners are relying largely on their own efforts, using basic machinery such as loaders to try to recover those killed or trapped beneath the rubble. Despite appeals to the relevant authorities for urgent intervention, there has so far been no recorded official response to the disaster, Ahmed says. Remote site under RSF control El Zara area is entirely controlled by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), Ahmed says. It is tightly sealed off and difficult to reach, creating an additional obstacle to the deployment of specialised rescue teams. More than 5,000 traditional miners are working at El Zara mine, according to Ahmed. Most moved to the area after the RSF captured El Nahud and much of Kordofan. Many turned to gold mining after losing their previous livelihoods in trade, pastoralism, and farming. For them, the mine has become a last resort for earning a living. State absence and safety risks Ahmed says there is almost no state presence at the mine, leaving workers without meaningful safety measures or protection. The area’s sandy terrain makes mine shafts particularly vulnerable to collapse once they reach certain depths, while inadequate safety precautions contribute to repeated accidents. The dangers extend beyond collapses. Reports warn of potential environmental and health risks from chemicals such as mercury and cyanide, which are used to extract gold and can cause illness among miners and nearby communities. Miners at Zara face serious risks every day without any authority overseeing their safety or helping them work in safer conditions, Ahmed says. Calls are growing for urgent intervention to rescue anyone still trapped and prevent further disasters of this kind. Note: This report has been translated from Arabic with the assistance of artificial intelligence tools, and subsequently reviewed and adapted by a human editor before publication. items.title: Yassir Zabiri réalise son rêve face au Barça et pointe les lacunes défensives de Santander
items.description: Entré en jeu face au FC Barcelone, Yassir Zabiri a marqué au Camp Nou malgré la lourde défaite du Racing Santander (7-2). L’international marocain, qui porte son total à six buts cette saison, a également souligné les difficultés défensives de son équipe. Yassir Zabiri a vécu une soirée particulière mercredi au Camp Nou. L’attaquant marocain du Racing Santander a réalisé un rêve d’enfance en affrontant le FC Barcelone dans son stade, avant de trouver le chemin des filets malgré la lourde défaite de son équipe (7-2). Entré en cours de match, Zabiri a profité du temps de jeu qui lui a été accordé pour inscrire l’un des deux buts de Santander. Une réalisation symbolique pour le joueur, qui n’a jamais caché son admiration pour le club catalan. « Je suis très heureux d’avoir joué au Camp Nou. Pour moi, c’est un rêve d’enfance qui s’est réalisé. C’est incroyable de marquer dans un match comme celui-ci » , a déclaré l’international marocain après la rencontre. « Tout le monde sait que j’aime Barcelone depuis mon enfance. Cette soirée est donc particulière pour moi, malgré la défaite » , a-t-il ajouté. Au-delà de sa satisfaction personnelle, Zabiri a toutefois reconnu les difficultés rencontrées par le Racing Santander sur le plan défensif. Selon lui, l’équipe affiche de solides qualités offensives, mais doit encore progresser dans son organisation collective. « Nous avons une attaque forte, mais nous souffrons de gros problèmes défensifs. Nous ne savons pas encore bien défendre collectivement et nous devons améliorer cet aspect », a-t-il expliqué. Avec ce nouveau but, Zabiri porte son total à six réalisations en six matchs depuis le début de la saison. Une dynamique qui confirme son excellent début d’exercice et lui permet de poursuivre sa progression avec le Racing Santander. Malgré le score lourd concédé face au Barça, cette rencontre restera donc particulière pour le jeune attaquant marocain, qui a non seulement découvert le Camp Nou, mais a également réussi à y inscrire son nom au tableau des buteurs. items.title: Santé : Okoumé Capital injecte 500 millions FCFA au Centre diagnotic de Libreville
items.description: Filiale du Fonds gabonais d’investissements stratégiques (FGIS), Okoumé Capital a officiellement engagé, le 16 septembre 2026, un investissement de 500 millions de francs CFA au profit du Centre diagnostic de Libreville. Ce financement doit notamment renforcer les capacités diagnostiques de l’établissement et accompagner son développement à travers de nouvelles implantations. Moment de la signature avec les deux responsables. (capture d'écran). © GabonReview Le Centre diagnostic de Libreville a officiellement bénéficié, le 16 septembre 2026, d’un investissement de 500 millions de francs CFA d’Okoumé Capital, filiale du Fonds gabonais d’investissements stratégiques (FGIS). L’opération vise à consolider les capacités techniques et médicales du centre, tout en accompagnant son expansion. Le financement doit notamment contribuer au développement du Village Santé d’Akanda, au renforcement des capacités diagnostiques ainsi qu’à l’ouverture de nouvelles implantations. Au-delà de l’apport financier, cette opération traduit la volonté d’Okoumé Capital d’accompagner des acteurs privés engagés dans le développement de l’offre sanitaire au Gabon. Renforcer les capacités diagnostiques Le financement doit prioritairement permettre de renforcer les capacités du laboratoire et du pôle imagerie du Centre diagnostique de Libreville. Deux secteurs essentiels dans la chaîne de prise en charge médicale, puisqu’ils conditionnent notamment la qualité et la rapidité du diagnostic. Pour Okoumé Capital, l’investissement dans les infrastructures et les services de santé participe directement au renforcement du capital humain. « Lorsqu'un pays dispose d'infrastructures médicales performantes, il renforce son capital humain, améliore la qualité de vie de sa population et crée les conditions d'une croissance plus durable » , a déclaré le directeur, Fabrice Assoumou Essono. Le patron d'Okoumé Capital a également souligné le rôle joué par le Centre diagnostique dans le système de santé gabonais : « Nous sommes particulièrement heureux d'accompagner aujourd'hui le Centre diagnostique de Libreville. Au fil des années, cet établissement a su démontrer son rôle essentiel dans la chaîne de prise en charge médicale au Gabon par la qualité de ses prestations, par son expertise technique et par l'engagement quotidien de ses équipes au service de ses patients ». Un accompagnement qui dépasse les 500 millions Pour le promoteur du Centre diagnostique de Libreville, cet investissement constitue moins un point de départ qu'une nouvelle étape dans la croissance de l'établissement. « L'investissement que nous signons aujourd'hui est important, mais ces 500 millions ne constituent pas le commencement de notre histoire » , a expliqué Joris Loyce Olympio Fanguinoveny, patron du Centre diagnostique de Libreville. « Ils accompagnent une organisation qui travaille tous les jours, qui soigne, qui investit, qui grandit depuis près de 10 ans » , a-t-il poursuivi. Créé autour d’une offre spécialisée dans le diagnostic médical, le Centre diagnostique entend ainsi poursuivre son développement avec l'appui de cet investissement. Le Village Santé d’Akanda dans le dispositif L’un des volets de l’opération concerne le Village Santé d’Akanda, qui doit bénéficier de l’accompagnement financier d’Okoumé Capital. Le projet s’inscrit dans une logique d’élargissement de l’offre sanitaire et de proximité des services de diagnostic. Le financement doit également permettre d’envisager de nouvelles implantations afin d’étendre progressivement les capacités du groupe. Pour Okoumé Capital, cette opération relève ainsi d’une démarche d’accompagnement de l’entrepreneuriat local dans le secteur de la santé. L’enjeu sera désormais de transformer cet apport de 500 millions de francs CFA en capacités supplémentaires, en équipements et en services susceptibles de contribuer à l’amélioration de la prise en charge des patients au Gabon. L’article Santé : Okoumé Capital injecte 500 millions FCFA au Centre diagnotic de Libreville est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Crise de Ceuta : débâcle cuisante du Maroc au Parlement européen
items.description: Malgré une mobilisation exceptionnelle de l’appareil diplomatique marocain et les démarches de plusieurs eurodéputés socialistes espagnols pour infléchir et édulcorer le projet de résolution du Parlement européen, la crise de Ceuta a désormais franchi le cadre bilatéral entre Madrid et Rabat pour s’imposer comme une question européenne. Un basculement politique majeur, dont les conséquences seront dommageables pour le Maroc . Crise de Ceuta : le Parlement européen adopte une résolution contre le Maroc Dans ce contexte, le Parlement européen vient d’adopter, par 339 voix contre 225 et 16 abstentions, la résolution intitulée « Attaques hybrides récentes et instrumentalisation des migrants à Ceuta ». Le texte condamne avec fermeté les entrées massives depuis le Maroc et qualifie l’instrumentalisation de la migration irrégulière d’outil de « guerre hybride » contre l’intégrité territoriale d’un État membre. Il demande à Rabat d’assumer ses responsabilités et de respecter ses engagements en matière de contrôle des frontières, de retours et de coopération migratoire. Sur le terrain financier, la résolution demande également à Bruxelles de mettre en place des mécanismes permettant de suspendre des versements à un pays tiers et de récupérer les fonds déjà versés en cas de défaut de coopération ou lorsque les intérêts de l’Union ou de ses États membres sont menacés. Cette évolution avait été préparée par le débat du 15 septembre au Parlement européen. La protection des frontières extérieures, « l’instrumentalisation des flux migratoires et les menaces hybrides » avaient été placées au cœur des échanges. Le rôle de Frontex et la coopération avec les pays tiers avaient également été évoqués. Le choix de ces termes a donné au dossier une dimension sécuritaire qui dépasse désormais celle d’une simple crise migratoire. Dans le même temps, la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a enfoncé le clou en donnant à cette évolution une portée politique supplémentaire, en déclarant : « Ceuta est Espagne. Ceuta est l’Europe. Et l’Europe sera à vos côtés. » Cette déclaration constitue un avertissement politique direct et ferme à l’adresse de Rabat, alors que les autorités espagnoles dénoncent les pressions et les manœuvres liées à la gestion des flux migratoires. Ce qui change pour Rabat À Bruxelles, le ministre espagnol des Affaires étrangères, José Manuel Albares, a à son tour porté le dossier en demandant notamment une présence permanente de Frontex à Ceuta et Melilla, et une prise en compte renforcée de la situation particulière de ces deux villes dans les politiques européennes. Au fond, le dossier de Ceuta et Melilla se trouve désormais placé au croisement de trois enjeux : la protection de la frontière extérieure de l’Union, l’instrumentalisation des flux migratoires et la réponse européenne aux menaces hybrides. À ce titre, la résolution marque une nouvelle étape dans l’européanisation du dossier de Ceuta. Pour Rabat, le changement ne tient pas seulement au vocabulaire employé à Strasbourg. Il se traduit aussi par la mise en place de mécanismes européens susceptibles de conditionner la coopération et les financements qui lui seraient accordés. Reste enfin à souligner l’exercice d’équilibriste des socialistes espagnols, dont la ligne consiste à reconnaître la gravité de la dimension sécuritaire de la crise tout en s’opposant au texte porté par la droite européenne, afin de préserver la relation avec Rabat et d’éviter de nouvelles crispations. *Ancien Ambassadeur L’article Crise de Ceuta : débâcle cuisante du Maroc au Parlement européen est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Guinée : France 24 interdite de diffusion avec effet immédiat par la Haute Autorité de la communication
items.description: La Haute Autorite de la communication (HAC), organe guineen de regulation des medias, a decide, a l'issue d'une seance extraordinaire tenue le 17 septembre, d'interdire avec effet immediat la diffusion de France 24 sur l'ensemble du territoire de la Republique de Guinee. La mesure concerne tous les vecteurs techniques, notamment le satellite, le câble, les applications mobiles, les sites Internet et les reseaux sociaux. La chaîne avait ete mise en demeure la veille par le meme organe, qui lui avait ordonne de « cesser immediatement l'usage de termes attentatoires a la dignite du chef de l'etat et de proceder aux rectifications editoriales requises ». La decision du 17 septembre, signee par le president de la HAC, Boubacar Yacine Diallo, invoque le « refus manifeste, delibere et caracterise » de France 24 de se conformer a cette injonction. ❗️ #Guinée : la Haute Autorité de la communication (HAC) met en demeure #France24 pour avoir utilisé « un qualificatif inapproprié » pour désigner le président guinéen Mamadi #Doumbouya . pic.twitter.com/04DQXvps6r — RT en français (@RTenfrancais) September 16, 2026 La HAC qualifie ce refus d'« insubordination », de « defi ouvert » a l'instance de regulation et d'« offense continue » a la personne du president guineen Mamadi Doumbouya. Elle y voit egalement une « violation flagrante de la souverainete juridique de la Republique de Guinee ». Retrait des accreditations et blocage des acces numeriques La decision revoque par ailleurs l'autorisation de diffusion de France 24 en Guinee et retire, avec effet immediat, les accreditations de presse de l'ensemble de ses correspondants, envoyes speciaux et collaborateurs dans le pays. La HAC a egalement requis l'Autorite de regulation des postes et telecommunications (ARPT) afin qu'elle procede sans delai au blocage de tous les acces numeriques a la chaîne, notamment ses sites Internet, ses flux de streaming et ses applications mobiles. Les autorites guineennes reprochent a France 24 l'emploi, dans une sequence diffusee le 15 septembre, de l'expression « president putschiste » jugee attentatoire a la dignite du president Mamadi Doumbouya. Un manquement grave et un choix delibere de la chaîne « d'ignorer la legitimite issue des urnes en employant un tel qualificatif a l'encontre d'un president de la Republique democratiquement elu », estime la HAC.

items.description: Guérin-Kouka, 17 sept. (ATOP) – Les membres de la Conférence administrative préfectorale (CAP) ont tenu leur session trimestrielle le mercredi 16 septembre à Guérin-Kouka. Cette rencontre, présidée par le préfet de Dankpen, Col. Akpamoura Koffi, président du comité, a regroupé les membres des collectivités territoriales, la chefferie traditionnelle et les services déconcentrés de l’Etat. Elle a permis d’échanger sur l’avancement des projets et programmes et projets de l’Etat dans la préfecture. La séance a été marquée par la lecture du rapport de la précédente conférence, les présentations des rapports de la préfecture, des trois communes, des directions de l’Action Sociale et de la Solidarité, de l’Environnement et des Travaux Publics. Ces différentes présentations portent sur l’état d’avancement des projets et programmes de l’Etat déjà réalisés, en cours de la réalisation, les difficultés rencontrées et les défis à relever. Le préfet Akpamoura a rappelé que la CAP est une instance de concertation, de coordination et d’évaluation de l’action publique au niveau préfectoral. Il a indiqué qu’elle constitue une occasion pour les membres de se retrouver pour une synergie d’action afin de contribuer au développement local. ATOP/BN/BA

items.description: Les experts en santé animale de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) ont tenu, du 14 au 16 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, un atelier consacré à la validation des documents devant servir à harmoniser et à renforcer la réponse aux maladies animales transfrontalières dans l’espace confédéral. Présidée par le camarade Hiver BOUSSINI, Conseiller technique du ministre délégué chargé des Ressources animales du Burkina Faso, cette rencontre traduit la volonté du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger de renforcer leur coopération face aux menaces sanitaires qui ignorent les frontières. L’objectif est de doter l’espace confédéral AES d’outils communs permettant d’anticiper les risques, de coordonner les interventions et, à terme, de consolider la souveraineté des trois États en matière de santé animale. À l’issue des travaux, trois instruments complémentaires ont été retenus. Le premier est un dispositif harmonisé de surveillance épidémiologique. Il doit faciliter le partage rapide des informations sanitaires entre les services vétérinaires des trois pays. Ainsi, lorsqu’une menace est détectée dans une partie de l’espace confédéral, l’alerte pourra être rapidement portée à la connaissance des autres États afin de permettre une intervention coordonnée avant que la maladie ne se propage. Cette capacité de détection et de réaction doit être soutenue par une disponibilité plus régulière des vaccins. C’est tout l’enjeu du deuxième instrument : la mise en place d’une banque confédérale de vaccins vétérinaires contre les maladies prioritaires. Elle vise notamment à répondre aux difficultés récurrentes liées à l’acquisition, à la programmation budgétaire et au financement des campagnes de vaccination. Elle permettra également de mieux organiser le transport, le stockage, le respect de la chaîne du froid et l’acheminement des doses, y compris vers les zones les plus reculées. Le troisième instrument porte sur l’organisation de campagnes de vaccination concertées. Il s’agit de dépasser la juxtaposition de campagnes nationales conduites selon des calendriers différents, particulièrement dans les zones frontalières. Une programmation coordonnée devrait ainsi favoriser une meilleure couverture vaccinale et réduire les risques de réintroduction ou de propagation des maladies d’un pays à l’autre. Cette approche commune se justifie par la forte mobilité des populations et des animaux entre les trois États. « Nos cheptels circulent, nos populations échangent et nos territoires constituent un même continuum écologique et économique. Il serait donc illusoire de prétendre contrôler efficacement les maladies animales dans un seul pays lorsque les facteurs de risque demeurent actifs de part et d’autre de nos frontières », a fait remarquer le camarade BOUSSINI. Il a, par ailleurs, salué la prise en compte de l’approche « 𝑂𝑛𝑒 𝐻𝑒𝑎𝑙𝑡ℎ », qui met en synergie la santé animale, la santé humaine et la protection de l’environnement. Une démarche qui permet d’appréhender les risques sanitaires de manière globale et de renforcer la prévention des maladies susceptibles d’affecter à la fois les animaux et les populations. Avant la clôture des travaux, une délégation des participants, conduite par le camarade Hiver BOUSSINI, a été reçue par le ministre délégué chargé des Ressources animales, le Dr Amadou DICKO. Les experts lui ont présenté l’état d’avancement des travaux et recueilli ses orientations pour la poursuite du processus. Le ministre DICKO a félicité les participants pour cette initiative et souligné la nécessité pour les trois pays de renforcer davantage les actions communes en faveur de la souveraineté de la Confédération. Il a également évoqué deux initiatives majeures en cours au Burkina Faso : l’ouverture prochaine d’un établissement de formation de médecins vétérinaires et la mise en place d’une unité de fabrication de médicaments vétérinaires. Pour le ministre, ces différentes initiatives, associées aux instruments en cours de validation, devraient contribuer à renforcer l’autonomie de l’espace confédéral, à améliorer la santé et la productivité animales et, par conséquent, à consolider la sécurité alimentaire. En rappel, cette rencontre s’inscrit dans la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route de l’An II de la Confédération AES, créée par le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger. Elle traduit la volonté des trois États de donner un contenu concret au principe de solidarité confédérale, en construisant des réponses communes à des défis sanitaires qui, par nature, dépassent les frontières nationales. 𝗗𝗖𝗥𝗣/𝗠𝗔𝗘𝗥𝗔𝗛

items.title: IPOB demands referendum on Nigeria’s political future
items.description: The Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, has called for a referendum to allow Nigerians and the various constituent peoples of the country to determine their preferred political future. In a statement signed by its spokesperson, Emma Powerful, the group argued that the 2027 general elections alone would not resolve what it described as longstanding constitutional and political questions in Nigeria. IPOB said it believed a referendum would provide an opportunity for the people to express their views on the structure and future of the country through a democratic process. The group referred to previous referendums in other countries, including the United Kingdom, as examples of how questions concerning political arrangements could be subjected to popular decision-making. IPOB also cited previous statements attributed to former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo and Goodluck Jonathan on the need to address Nigeria’s political and constitutional challenges. According to the group, elections and referendums serve different purposes, with elections focusing on the choice of political office holders, while a referendum could allow citizens to directly decide a specific constitutional or political question. IPOB questioned why its demand for a referendum on self-determination should be treated differently from other calls for popular consultation on the future of a country. The group therefore urged the Federal Government and other stakeholders to consider a peaceful and democratic process through which the various constituent peoples of Nigeria could express their preferences on the country’s political structure and future. It stressed that its position, as presented in the statement, was a call for a political and democratic process rather than an endorsement of violence. IPOB called on Nigerians to engage the issue through dialogue and other lawful democratic means. The post IPOB demands referendum on Nigeria’s political future appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LE CHP-Sotouboua valide son rapport d’orientation stratégique du PEH 2026-2030
items.description: Sotouboua, 17 sept. (ATOP) – Le rapport d’orientation stratégique et des perspectives du Projet d’établissement hospitalier (PEH) 2026-2030 du Centre hospitalier préfectoral (CHP) de Sotouboua a été validé par les acteurs réunis en atelier, les 14 et 15 septembre à Sotouboua. L’atelier s’inscrit dans la dynamique de l’amélioration de la gouvernance, de la qualité des soins et des performances de cet hôpital. Il a permis aux participants d’examiner le rapport, d’apprécier les différents éléments qui le composent et de formuler des observations et propositions en vue de son amélioration. Les travaux ont notamment porté sur l’analyse de la situation du CHP, l’identification des principaux défis auxquels l’établissement est confronté ainsi que la définition des grandes orientations devant guider son développement sur la période 2026-2030. Les échanges ont également permis de dégager des perspectives visant à renforcer l’offre de soins, la qualité des prestations et la satisfaction des usagers. A l’issue des échanges, le document a été validé après prise en compte des différentes observations. Cette étape constitue une avancée majeure vers la finalisation du PEH du CHP de Sotouboua. Les travaux ont été dirigés par le consultant Agoudavi Kokou. Le président du conseil d’administration dudit hôpital et maire de la commune Sotouboua 1, Gnanguissa Plibam s’est félicité de la validation de ce rapport qui constitue, selon lui, un outil important de planification et de développement de cet hôpital. Le directeur du CHP, Agbaguede Alassane, a souligné qu’à travers ce projet, leur formation sanitaire entend disposer d’une feuille de route claire pour l’amélioration de la prise en charge sanitaire des populations pour les cinq prochaines années. Le directeur régional de la Santé du centre, Dr N’djao Akawulu et le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Sotouboua, Akakpo Nyagoulamba ont réaffirmé leur engagement à accompagner le CHP dans la mise en œuvre de son projet. ATOP/BTP/MEK/BA
